**Visual observations on test image:**
- Single tomato leaf with fine white/silvery stippling/speckling uniformly distributed across the entire upper surface
- Leaf shape is intact, no large lesions, brown spots, or target rings
- Dull, mottled appearance — consistent with chlorophyll removal by piercing feeding
- No obvious yellowing zones, no concentric rings, no powdery coating

**Matching against candidates:**
- The fine, uniform stippling pattern is the hallmark of **Spider Mites** — mites suck chlorophyll out of cells, creating tiny pale flecks
- No concentric rings → rules out Early_Blight, Target_Spot
- No powdery white coating → rules out Powdery_Mildew
- No brown/water-soaked lesions → rules out Bacterial_Spot, Late_Blight
- No mosaic/mottling discoloration → rules out virus classes

**Reference comparison:** The Spider_Mites reference images show the same fine stippling + dull leaf texture on an otherwise intact leaf — matches the test image well.
